title: Simplest cudagraph model fails on second backward pass (unless cudagraph_trees is disabled)

labels.name: module: cuda graphs
labels.description: Ability to capture and then replay streams of CUDA kernels

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

I was trying to see if torch.compile's reduce-overhead could help me, but found that even when pared back to a minimal model (one Linear layer): I couldn't do two forward+backward passes on the model instance.

However if I disable `torch._inductor.config.triton.cudagraph_trees`, it can be made to work.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn, Tensor

# uncomment these to make it work, at the cost of losing some re-use capability
# import torch._inductor.config
# torch._inductor.config.triton.cudagraph_trees = False

device = torch.device("cuda")

hp_dtype=torch.bfloat16

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.proj = nn.Linear(out_features=dim, in_features=dim, bias=False, dtype=hp_dtype)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor):
        y = self.proj(x)
        return y

dim=768

with torch.device('meta'):
    model = Model(dim=dim)
seed=42
gen=torch.Generator(device)
loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()

model.to_empty(device=device)
model.proj.weight.data.normal_(std=dim**-.5, generator=gen.manual_seed(seed))

model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, fullgraph=True, mode='reduce-overhead')

microbsz = 131072
input = torch.randn((1, microbsz, dim), device=device, dtype=hp_dtype, generator=gen.manual_seed(seed+1), requires_grad=True)
target = torch.randn((1, microbsz, dim), device=device, dtype=hp_dtype, generator=gen.manual_seed(seed+2))

def with_cudagraph_do_fwdbwd(mod: Model):
    torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin()
    out: Tensor = mod(input.clone()).clone()
    loss: Tensor = loss_fn(out, target)
    loss.backward()

with_cudagraph_do_fwdbwd(model)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
model.zero_grad()
# gets past first fwdbwd just fine

# fails on .backward() of this subsequent invocation
with_cudagraph_do_fwdbwd(model)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

```
RuntimeError: Error: accessing tensor output of CUDAGraphs that has been overwritten by a subsequent run. Stack trace: File "/mnt/clusterstorage/workspace/mahouko/git/modded-nanogpt-priv/repro.py", line 19, in forward
    y = self.proj(x). To prevent overwriting, clone the tensor outside of torch.compile() or call torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin() before each model invocation.
```
